Playbook.name: Change Audit — FortiGate Administrator Login from a New Source - SOC Playbook

Metadata.Category: Change Audit — Valid Accounts (Anomalous Admin Access)

ExecutiveSummary.Overview: A FortiGate administrator successfully logged in from a source that has not been seen for admin logins before (new-terms on the login source). The triage question: is this a legitimate admin working from a new but authorised location (new workstation, VPN pool, jump host), or is it unauthorised use of valid administrator credentials to reach the firewall management plane? This is a change-audit / anomalous-access signal, low severity by default, whose weight rises sharply if the new source then makes configuration changes or shows credential-guessing behaviour. Verified live: FortiGate login events carry user.name, source.ip and event.outcome ("success"); fortinet.firewall.status is null on logins, so success/failure is read from event.outcome. Baseline example: admin "and" normally logs in from 192.168.193.10 (the management workstation).
ExecutiveSummary.BusinessImpact: Administrative access to the FortiGate cluster controls the bank's perimeter and internal segmentation. Valid-account misuse against the firewall management plane is a foothold to weaken defenses, open ingress, or observe/redirect traffic — so an admin session from an unexpected source deserves confirmation even when the login itself succeeded.

Assets.AssetType: FortiGate firewall cluster (JCB-FGT-Primary / JCB-FGT-Secondary) management plane

LogSources.LogSource: FortiGate event log — logs-fortinet_fortigate.log-* (verified live: fortinet.firewall.action "login" with user.name, source.ip, event.outcome, observer.name populated; status null on login)

TelemetryRequirements.Requirement: FortiGate admin login events shipped to logs-fortinet_fortigate.log-* (verified live).
Success/failure is read from event.outcome ("success"/other), NOT fortinet.firewall.status which is null on login events (verified live).

The "new source" determination is historical (new-terms baseline of admin login sources). Within a 4-hour investigation window you will typically see only the new source; compare against the admin's known-good sources / the baseline the rule used.

Signal.Name: Admin login from a new source
Signal.Details: fortinet.firewall.action "login" by a user.name from a source.ip not previously seen for admin logins, event.outcome "success", on a FortiGate (observer.name).

Signal.Name: Escalating follow-on
Signal.Details: Config changes attributable to the new source (ui="GUI(<source>)"), or failed logins / multiple accounts from the same source, turn an anomalous login into a likely intrusion.

Input.name: $admin
Input.description: The administrator account that logged in (user.name from the alert).

Input.name: $source_ip
Input.description: The new source address the admin logged in from (source.ip from the alert).

ImmediateCapture.Item: Device (observer.name) and login outcome from the alert

InitialAssessment.Rule: If $source_ip maps to a known admin location (management subnet, VPN pool, a newly-provisioned admin workstation) and $admin regularly administers the firewall, lean legitimate new location (False Positive / authorised).
If the new source then makes config changes (INV-02), or the source shows failed logins / multiple admin accounts (INV-03), or $source_ip is outside any admin network, escalate.

Investigation.Goal: Decide whether the admin login from the new source is legitimate authorised access from a new location or unauthorised valid-account use, by profiling the admin's login pattern and checking for follow-on configuration changes and credential-guessing from the source.

Step.name: Profile the admin's recent login sources and outcomes
Step.Purpose: Establish $admin's login pattern in the window — which sources, success/failure, which devices — so the new source stands out against the admin's normal behaviour.
Step.Query: FROM logs-fortinet_fortigate.log-* | WHERE fortinet.firewall.action == "login" AND user.name == "$admin" AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | STATS logins = COUNT(*), outcomes = VALUES(event.outcome), devices = VALUES(observer.name), first_seen = MIN(@timestamp), last_seen = MAX(@timestamp) BY source.ip | SORT logins DESC | LIMIT 20
Step.AnalystNotes: Compare the new $source_ip against the admin's other sources here and against the known-good baseline (e.g. the management workstation 192.168.193.10). A single successful login from a plausible admin subnet is likely benign; the new source appearing alongside failures, or being the admin's only activity from an unusual network, is more concerning.

Step.name: Did the new source make configuration changes
Step.Purpose: The decisive escalation check: a new-source admin session that proceeds to change firewall config is far higher-risk than a login alone. Config changes carry the operator in fortinet.firewall.ui as "GUI(<source>)".
Step.Query: FROM logs-fortinet_fortigate.log-* | WHERE fortinet.firewall.action IN ("Add","Edit","Delete") AND fortinet.firewall.ui LIKE "*$source_ip*" AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | KEEP @timestamp, observer.name, fortinet.firewall.cfgpath, fortinet.firewall.cfgattr, fortinet.firewall.ui | SORT @timestamp DESC | LIMIT 25
Step.AnalystNotes: Any high-impact change (firewall.policy, address objects, system.admin/api-user, admin trusted-host/access) made from the new source turns this into a probable intrusion — pivot to the "Potential Unauthorized Changes" response. No changes keeps it an access-only anomaly to verify with the admin.

Step.name: Check the new source for credential-guessing or multi-account use
Step.Purpose: Distinguish a benign new admin location from an attacker source: failed logins before success, or several admin accounts attempted from the same source, indicate credential access rather than a legitimate move.
Step.Query: FROM logs-fortinet_fortigate.log-* | WHERE fortinet.firewall.action == "login" AND source.ip == "$source_ip" AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | STATS attempts = COUNT(*), users = VALUES(user.name), devices = VALUES(observer.name), last_seen = MAX(@timestamp) BY event.outcome | SORT attempts DESC | LIMIT 15
Step.AnalystNotes: A single successful login for one admin account from the source is consistent with a legitimate new location. Failed attempts preceding success, or multiple distinct admin usernames tried from the same source, is credential-guessing / spraying against the management plane and should be escalated regardless of the eventual outcome.

Node.Condition: INV-02 shows the new source made firewall configuration changes (especially high-impact policy/address/admin-access changes) with no change ticket.
Node.Result: True Positive (Valid-account misuse leading to firewall change — escalate to IR)

Node.Condition: INV-03 shows failed logins preceding success, or multiple admin accounts attempted from $source_ip, or $source_ip is outside any authorised admin network.
Node.Result: True Positive (Credential access / unauthorised admin-plane access — escalate to IR)

Node.Condition: INV-01/INV-03 show a single successful login for $admin from a source that maps to a known admin location (management subnet, VPN pool, newly-provisioned admin workstation), with no follow-on changes and no failures.
Node.Result: False Positive (Authorised admin access from a new but legitimate location)

Node.Condition: The new source is a newly-added but sanctioned admin path (e.g. a new jump host or NAT egress) whose baseline simply has not caught up.
Node.Result: Misconfiguration (Baseline gap — record the new legitimate source; do not disable the analytic)

Node.Condition: $source_ip cannot be attributed to a known admin location and no follow-on activity yet confirms intent.

FalsePositive.Definition: A known administrator legitimately logged in from a new but authorised location — the source must be tied to a sanctioned admin network/workstation, not merely assumed benign because the login succeeded.

Indicators.Item: $source_ip maps to a management subnet, VPN pool, or a newly-provisioned admin workstation (confirmable with the admin/network team).
Single successful login for $admin, no failed attempts and no other accounts from the source (INV-03).

SOCAction.Item: Confirm the new location with $admin / network team; close as false_positive.
If the source is a permanent new admin path, record it so the baseline recognises it going forward.

TruePositive.Definition: Valid administrator credentials were used from an unauthorised source to reach the firewall management plane — for access, credential-guessing, or to make configuration changes.

Indicators.Item: Follow-on firewall config changes from the new source (INV-02).
Failed logins before success, or multiple admin accounts tried from the source (INV-03).
Source outside any authorised admin network / geolocation.

SOCAction.Item: Treat $admin's credentials as potentially compromised; force a credential reset and review FortiGate admin sessions.
Restrict admin access to trusted-host management IPs; if changes were made, revert them and follow the unauthorised-change response; hunt for the source elsewhere in the estate.

Misconfiguration.Definition: A sanctioned but newly-introduced admin path (new jump host, changed NAT/VPN egress) tripped the new-source baseline — legitimate, just not yet learned.

Indicators.Item: The source is confirmed as a new authorised admin egress/host.
Behaviour is otherwise normal (single success, no changes or authorised changes).

SOCAction.Item: Record the new legitimate source; keep the analytic enabled so genuinely new sources still alert.

Phase.name: Immediate Actions (0-30 minutes)
Phase.Action: Attribute $source_ip (INV-01/INV-03) — is it a known admin location? Check INV-02 for any configuration changes from the source.
If the source is unauthorised or config changes were made, treat $admin as compromised: force credential reset and review active FortiGate admin sessions.

Phase.name: Containment and Eradication (hours)
Phase.Action: Revert any unauthorised changes made from the source; restrict FortiGate admin access to trusted management IPs; rotate admin credentials/API keys as needed.
Review the source for wider activity (other devices/services) and contain it; reconstruct the admin session timeline.

Phase.name: Recovery and Hardening (days)
Phase.Action: Enforce admin trusted-host restrictions and MFA for FortiGate administration; define the authorised admin source set.
Maintain the new-source baseline and pair this analytic with the config-change analytic for higher-confidence correlated detection.

Escalation.Trigger: Follow-on config changes from the new source, credential-guessing / multi-account attempts from the source, or a source that cannot be attributed to an authorised admin location.

FalsePositiveClosure.Item: New source confirmed as an authorised admin location by the admin/network team.
Single successful login, no follow-on changes and no credential-guessing; new legitimate source recorded for the baseline.

TruePositiveClosure.Item: $admin credentials reset and admin sessions reviewed; unauthorised changes reverted; trusted-host restrictions applied.
Source contained and hunted across the estate; incident documented.
